text: Writing clean code is a valuable skill that makes life easier for you and anyone else who reads your work. The most important goal is readability. Your code should tell a story that is easy to follow, even for someone seeing it for the first time. One key way to achieve this is by using clear naming conventions. A variable named `userAge` is much better than `u`, because it instantly explains what it holds. Similarly, functions should have descriptive names and do one thing well. For example, a function called `calculateTotalPrice` is far more useful than a long, complicated block of code. By breaking your program into small, focused functions, you improve its maintainability. When a bug appears, or you need to add a new feature, you can easily find the right spot to change without breaking the whole system. In short, clean code is simple, direct, and a pleasure to work with.
